post.summary: Create book
post.description:
CASE (course_id/unit_id set vs both null):
- course_id and/or unit_id SET -> this is a course/unit-bundled book: price is FORCED to 0.00 server-side no matter what you send, and students can ONLY access it via their course/unit subscription (POST /student/books/subscribe will actively REJECT a standalone purchase attempt on it).

CASE (allow_download): 1 (default) = student gets a direct downloadable link; 0 = file_path/link are hidden from the student response entirely and they must use GET /student/books/stream instead.

post.summary: Create session (update-1: days[] batch create)
post.description:
CASE (validation path depends on which of course_id/subject_id is sent):
- course_id set -> validated as a COURSE session: rejected if the teacher isn't assigned to that course, or if another teacher already owns it. EXCEPTION (update-1): if the course has NEITHER an assigned teacher NOR a subject_id (e.g. a content-free package with no teacher pinned yet), ANY teacher is allowed - this lets a different teacher be picked per session/day on the same course.
- course_id empty + subject_id set -> validated as a SUBJECT session: rejected if the teacher isn't assigned to that subject for the given academic_year_id (grade).
CASE (academic_year_id): null/omitted = session is open to ALL grades; a specific id = session is grade-locked and only shows to students of that exact grade (see /student/sessions/today).
CASE (update-1, days vs day_of_week): if `days` (array) is sent, one class_sessions row is inserted per day in one call (all other fields shared) and `data` returns an ARRAY of created sessions; if only `day_of_week` is sent (legacy, unchanged), `data` returns a single object exactly as before.

subject_id.description: CASE: used for validation only when course_id is empty — see operation description

course_id.description: CASE: when set, takes precedence over subject_id for validation — see operation description

day_of_week.description: Legacy single-day create — still supported and still returns a single object, not an array

days.description: update-1: optional — pick multiple days to create the same recurring session on all of them in one call, e.g. attaching a full weekly schedule to a course at once. Takes precedence over day_of_week when present.

put.summary: Review a reschedule request (NEW: teacher reassignment + time override on approval)
put.description:
CASE (decision=rejected): only id/decision/admin_note matter, everything else below is ignored.
CASE (decision=approved, 3 sub-scenarios):
1) Default (no keep_original_schedule, no new_day/time overrides) -> applies the teacher's own originally-requested new_day/new_start_time/new_end_time as-is.
2) new_day/new_start_time/new_end_time sent -> OVERRIDES the teacher's requested time with the admin's own choice instead.
3) keep_original_schedule=true -> ignores any new day/time entirely, keeps the session at its CURRENT day/time, and instead REASSIGNS it to new_teacher_id (which becomes REQUIRED in this case and is validated against that teacher's course/subject+grade assignment).

keep_original_schedule.description: NEW: keep original day/time, reassign teacher instead (requires new_teacher_id)

post.summary: Create exam
post.description:
CASE (3 scenarios, decided by which of course_id/unit_id/subject_id you send):
1) course_id ONLY -> exam applies to the WHOLE course (all units) — unit_id must be omitted/null.
2) course_id + unit_id -> exam is scoped to that ONE unit inside the course only — students only see it while inside that unit.
3) course_id + subject_id (course spans multiple subjects) -> further narrows the whole-course exam to just that subject's students.
subject_id and unit_id can be combined with course_id independently; there is no exam scoped by subject_id alone without a course_id.

course_id.description: REQUIRED in all cases — every exam belongs to a course

unit_id.description: CASE: omit/null = exam covers the whole course. Set = exam is scoped to only this unit within course_id.

subject_id.description: CASE: only meaningful when the course itself spans multiple subjects — narrows a whole-course exam to one subject's students.

post.summary: Create question (NEW: order_num, mcq_options alias, written type)
post.description:
CASE 1 (scope resolution): course_id/unit_id/subject_id are OPTIONAL — if omitted, the server auto-resolves them from exam_id (inherits whatever course/unit/subject the parent exam itself belongs to, see /admin/exams cases above). Only send them explicitly to override; if the course can't be resolved at all (bad exam_id), the request fails with 422.
CASE 2 (question_type decides which answer-fields are used, others are ignored/must be omitted):
- question_type=mcq -> use mcq_options[] (each option has is_correct); correct_answer and model_answer_* are ignored.
- question_type=true_false -> use correct_answer (0 or 1); mcq_options and model_answer_* are ignored.
- question_type=written -> use model_answer_ar/model_answer_en/model_answer (for reference/manual grading); mcq_options and correct_answer are ignored, this type is NOT auto-graded.

subject_id.description: CASE: optional, auto-resolved from exam_id if omitted

post.summary: update-1 (NEW): Validate a subscription code before registration (no account yet)
post.description: update-1 (NEW): First step of "join with a code" flow. No auth required. Validates the code (exists, active, within valid_from/valid_to, under max_uses) WITHOUT consuming it or creating any account. On success returns a short-lived (30 min) onboarding_token (JWT, student-scoped, purpose=student_onboarding) that must be sent as Bearer token to /student/onboard/complete. This token cannot be used on any normal student-authenticated endpoint.

post.summary: update-1 (NEW): Complete profile and register as a student, auto-applying the code's subscription
post.description: update-1 (NEW): Second step. Auth: Bearer onboarding_token from /student/onboard/start (NOT a normal student session token — verified separately, purpose must be student_onboarding). Body is identical to normal /student/register (name/email/password required, phone/age/school_id/city_id/academic_year_id/study_language optional). Internally calls the same studentRegister() used by normal registration, then immediately redeems the onboarding code for the new student (subscription + subscription_status added to the response). Response then continues through the EXISTING email-OTP verification flow exactly like normal registration (verification.otp_code/expires_at, tokens).

200.description: OK — same shape as /student/register, plus subscription/subscription_status

subscription.description: update-1 (NEW): result of auto-redeeming the code for this new student

subscription_status.description: update-1 (NEW): success/error of the auto-redeem step

post.summary: update-1 (NEW): Validate a subscription code already claimed by a student, before parent registration
post.description: update-1 (NEW): First step of "join with a code" flow for a parent. No auth required. Requires the code to already have claimed_by_student_id set (i.e. some student already completed /student/onboard/complete or redeemed it) — otherwise returns an error asking the child to activate the code first. On success returns a short-lived (30 min) onboarding_token (JWT, parent-scoped, purpose=parent_onboarding, carries the bound student_id) plus the linked student's {id, name} for a confirmation UI.

400.description: Invalid code, or code not yet activated by any student

post.summary: update-1 (NEW): Complete profile, register as a parent, and auto-link to the code's student
post.description: update-1 (NEW): Second step. Auth: Bearer onboarding_token from /parent/onboard/start (NOT a normal parent session token — verified separately, purpose must be parent_onboarding). Body is identical to normal /parent/register (name/email/password required, city_id optional) — no student_id needed in the body, it comes from the token. Internally calls parentRegister(), then inserts a parent_students link row to the student bound in the token. Response adds linked_student_id. Unlike student onboarding, parent login has no OTP gate in this app, so the frontend logs the parent in immediately after this call.

post.summary: update-1: Redeem a subscription code as a logged-in student
post.description: update-1: request/response shape unchanged, but on the FIRST successful redemption of a given code by ANY student, the code's claimed_by_student_id is now permanently set (first claimer wins, never overwritten by later redemptions of the same multi-use code). This is what lets /parent/onboard/start later find which student to link a parent to. Course access granted by a subject_ids or teacher_ids code is scoped to the redeeming student's own academic_year_id (a course with academic_year_id=NULL stays visible to everyone). update-2 (Student): the resulting subscription's type is now 'package' (instead of always 'course') when every course the code is linked to has kind='package'. NOTE for API consumers creating codes (see POST /admin/subscription-codes): if a code is created with NO course_ids/subject_ids/teacher_ids linked at all, redeeming it here returns success but the message is "this activation code isn't linked to any content" and no access is granted — always send at least one of those three arrays when creating a code.

get.summary: (NEW) List the automatic system notifications addressed to the logged-in admin
get.description: Separate module (app/admin/notifications/inbox.php) from the existing send/history endpoints — this is what the admin RECEIVES (new student registration, course subscription, book purchase request, session started, consultation created), not what they sent. TEST CYCLE (real data from the latest DB dump): 1) POST /admin/auth/login with a real admin email (e.g. info@najeh.com, id=1, role=super_admin — password is hashed in the dump, you must supply the real plaintext yourself) to get an admin Bearer token. 2) Fire the event: POST /user/student/auth/login with {email:"omartalaat1276@gmail.com", password:"12345678"} (real, active student id=1065), then POST /student/subscriptions/redeem-code with {code:"123456789102"} using that student's token — this is a real, still-valid, unused-by-this-student code granting courses 201+202 (teacher id 201) and fires notify_of_course_subscription() for real. 3) Call this endpoint with the admin token to see the resulting notification. update-2 (Admin + Teacher): the "new subscription" notification's title/body now say "باقة"/"package" instead of always "كورس"/"course" when the subscribed course has kind='package' (including the correct Arabic possessive form, e.g. "باقتك" not "كورسك"). Same wording fix applies to the equivalent push notification sent to the course's teacher — no field/shape change, text content only.

get.summary: update-2: List the logged-in student's subscribed courses/packages with progress (bugfix: kind + teachers restored)
get.description: update-2 (Student): fixes a real production bug — this route's handler function was defined twice in the codebase (a duplicate `function_exists`-guarded copy in a different file was loading first and silently winning), so two things were missing from every response even though the fix had been written and deployed elsewhere: (1) the `kind` field ('normal' | 'package') was always absent from each course row, and (2) `teachers` was missing entirely. Both are now present on every item, sourced from the SAME shared helper used by the admin/teacher course-details endpoints, so the shape matches exactly. No change to auth, pagination, or any other field — safe to just start reading `kind` and `teachers[]` on this endpoint now.

post.summary: update-2 (NEW): Create a repeating weekly consultation slot for the logged-in teacher, bounded by an end date
post.description: update-2 (Teacher): companion to the existing single-slot POST /teacher/consultations. Instead of creating one dated slot, this materializes one consultation_slots row PER matching calendar date for every selected weekday between today and end_date (inclusive) — e.g. days=[Saturday,Thursday] with end_date next month creates one slot for every upcoming Saturday and every upcoming Thursday up to that date, all at the same slot_time. Safety caps: end_date cannot be more than 180 days out, and a single call cannot generate more than 200 dates total (split into multiple calls if needed). Any date that would collide with an existing (teacher_id, slot_time, slot_date) slot is silently skipped, not duplicated or erroring the whole request — the response reports how many were created vs skipped. Exactly ONE notification is sent for the whole batch (not one per generated slot).

days.description: one or more weekdays to repeat on; at least one required

slot_time.description: HH:MM, shared by every generated date

end_date.description: last date (inclusive) to generate slots up to; max 180 days from today

skipped_count.description: dates skipped because an identical slot already existed

400.description: No day selected / missing time or end_date / end_date in the past or beyond 180 days / more than 200 dates would be generated

Returns an error if teacher_id doesn't reference an existing teacher.

A 'package' course is just a course row with no units/videos/exams attached — it is organized around a weekly `class_sessions` schedule (see GET /admin/sessions and GET /teacher/sessions, both course_id-filterable, update-1) plus the existing course-files feature, instead of curriculum content.

kind.description: update-2 (NEW): defaults to 'normal' when omitted, so every pre-update-2 integration keeps creating plain courses unless it explicitly opts into 'package'.

put.summary: update-2 (NEW doc): Update a course or package, including switching its kind
put.description: update-2 (Admin): only `kind`, when present in the body, is new; every other field is pre-existing and updates only when present (partial update semantics), unchanged.

kind.description: update-2 (NEW): omit to leave kind unchanged; invalid values are silently ignored (kind stays whatever it already was).

get.summary: update-2 (NEW doc): Course details (now includes kind)
get.description: update-2 (Admin): the only new field is `kind` ('normal' | 'package'), defaulting to 'normal'. Everything else in this response (teachers[], subject, category, academic_year, created_by) is pre-existing, unchanged.

get.summary: update-2 (NEW doc): List the logged-in teacher's own courses (now kind-filterable)
get.description: update-2 (Teacher): thin wrapper around GET /admin/courses pre-scoped to this teacher (teacher_id forced server-side) — same `kind` filter/field applies, same response shape.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: update-2 (NEW): same semantics as GET /admin/courses

post.summary: update-2 (NEW doc): Create a course or package as a teacher (own subject only)
post.description: update-2 (Teacher): same new `kind` field as POST /admin/courses; unlike admin, subject_id is required and must already be assigned to this teacher. The created course is auto-linked to this teacher.

400.description: subject_id not assigned to this teacher, or name_ar missing

put.summary: update-2 (NEW doc): Update own course/package (including kind)
put.description: update-2 (Teacher): thin wrapper around PUT /admin/courses after an ownership check; same new `kind` field.

400.description: Not owner/assigned teacher of this course

get.summary: update-2: Public course/package listing (works logged-out; kind-filterable)
get.description: update-2 (Student, works with or without a token — StudentAuth optional): the only new things are the `kind` filter/field. When a student token IS sent, each row also gets `is_own`/`is_subscribed` as before (pre-existing behavior, unrelated to this update). BUGFIX (update-2): on this exact route the `kind` filter/field had briefly stopped working in production — a second, stale copy of this same handler function existed in another file and was silently shadowing the fixed one because it happened to load first. Fixed by patching the copy that actually runs; behavior now matches this doc. Alias: GET /student/courses is the exact same handler, exact same params/response.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: update-2 (NEW): omit to get both kinds mixed together in one list, each row carrying its own `kind`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: curriculum type filter (arabic/english/french/recorded) — unrelated to kind, pre-existing

get.summary: update-2: Alias of GET /courses (identical handler, params and response)
get.description: update-2: kept as a separate path only because both existed already; not a different implementation. See GET /courses for the full description of the kind filter/field and the shadowing bugfix.

get.summary: update-2: Course/package details page (now includes kind)
get.description: update-2 (Student, works with or without a token — StudentAuth optional): the only new field is `kind` ('normal' | 'package'). Everything else in this response (curriculum/units, teacher, subject, academic_year, price/discount) is pre-existing, unchanged. CASE (mobile integration guidance, not a schema change): when `kind` is 'package', expect `units`/curriculum to be empty by convention — instead fetch that package's weekly schedule from GET /student/sessions/today?course_id={id}&day=all (works pre-subscription as a read-only preview, see update-2 note on that endpoint) and its downloadable files from the existing course-files endpoints. Alias: GET /student/courses/show is the exact same handler, accepts the same `id`/`slug` query params.

get.summary: update-2: Alias of GET /courses/show (identical handler, params and response)
get.description: update-2: kept as a separate path only because both existed already; not a different implementation. See GET /courses/show for the full description of the kind field and package integration guidance.
